slides.title: Transition words: the ==4-second== decision
slides.hand: decide the relationship before you read the choices

slides.title: Opposite directions
slides.body: Use these only when the two sentences pull in opposite directions. Expected one thing, got another? That is contrast.
slides.tip: The SAT's favorite — it appears on almost every module

slides.title: Result, not restatement
slides.body: Use these only when the second sentence is a *result* of the first. If it just repeats the idea in new words, you need "in other words" instead.

slides.stem: The scientists expected the coral to bleach in the warmer water; ______, it thrived.
slides.prompt: Most students answer in under 5 seconds. Comment yours.

slides.trapWhy: "similarly" is the skim bait. It assumes the second sentence agrees with the first.
slides.intro: Name the direction between the two sentences first.
steps: Sentence 1 sets up an expectation: bleaching
